title: Herb-Butter Roast Turkey Breast
subtitle: a juicy boneless turkey breast under garlic and dried-herb butter, with real pan gravy — Christmas dinner without the whole bird
imageAlt: Sliced herb-butter roast turkey breast on a white platter with a small jug of pan gravy
servingsNote: Christmas dinner for two, plus 4 portions for turkey sandwiches

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen roast? Thaw it in its wrapper in the fridge, about 10 hours per kg — start the day before.
Oven at 190°C (375°F), rack in the lower middle so the top browns without scorching.
Have an instant-read thermometer ready — it comes out at 74°C (165°F), not by the clock.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Unwrap the roast (set aside any gravy packet for another day), leave the netting on and pat it very dry with paper towel.

steps.title: Make the herb butter
steps.text: Mash the soft butter with the garlic, dried herbs and paprika until evenly mixed.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Season the roast all over with the salt and pepper, then spread the herb butter over the top and sides. Lay the onion rings in a small roasting pan or 9×13 dish, set the roast on top and pour the broth around it.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast uncovered, basting with the pan juices every 30 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 74°C (165°F): about 1¼–1½ hours for a 1.4 kg roast (roughly 55 minutes per kg). If the top browns too fast, lay a loose sheet of foil over it.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Move the roast to a board, tent loosely with foil and rest 15 minutes so the juices settle back into the meat.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Pour the pan juices through a sieve into a measuring cup, pressing on the onions, and spoon off the fat. Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes until light golden. Whisk in the pan juices, broth and Worcestershire a little at a time until smooth, then simmer 4–5 minutes until it coats a spoon. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Carve
steps.text: Snip off the netting and slice the turkey about 1 cm thick. Serve with the hot gravy.

fixIt.fix: Lay foil loosely over the top and keep roasting in 10-minute stretches. Lower the rack one notch next time.
It went well past 74°C. Slice thinner, spoon warm gravy over, and pull it right at 74°C next time — it climbs a few degrees while resting.
Whisk hard for 30 seconds, or pour it through the sieve. Adding the liquid gradually prevents it.
Simmer 3–4 minutes more, or whisk in 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water and bubble 1 minute.

saleTip: Frozen boneless turkey breast roasts go on sale at No Frills in December, often $15–18. Buy two and keep one in the freezer for January.
swap: Bone-in turkey breast (about 2 kg): same herb butter, roast at 180°C (350°F) for 1½–2 hours to 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part, not touching the bone.
leftovers: Turkey sandwiches with cranberry sauce, hot turkey and gravy over toast, or chopped into a pot pie.
doneness: 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part of the breast (Health Canada, poultry pieces). It rises a few degrees while it rests. Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested boneless turkey breast roast methods (Turkey Farmers of Canada, Butterball roasting guides): roasted at 190°C (375°F) to 74°C (165°F) and rested, with a classic roux pan gravy.
prepAhead: Make the herb butter up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge; let it soften before spreading.
Move the frozen roast to the fridge 1–2 days before Christmas dinner.
reheat: Lay slices in a dish with a few spoonfuls of gravy or broth, cover with foil and warm at 160°C (325°F) about 20 minutes, until 74°C (165°F). Microwave single plates covered, 1–2 minutes.

basic.note: Butter, dried thyme, salt and pepper, and a quick gravy from the pan juices.

stepNotes.1: Basic: mash the butter with the dried thyme and paprika only.

fancy.note: A bacon blanket keeps the breast extra juicy, and a splash of cream makes the gravy silky.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: after the herb butter, lay the bacon strips side by side over the top, tucking the ends under.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: if the bacon is crisp before the turkey reaches 74°C, cover it loosely with foil.
stepNotes.5: Fancy: whisk in the cream for the last minute of simmering.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Carve through the bacon so every slice keeps a crisp strip. Pour the gravy into a warmed jug.

plating: Fan the slices down a warm platter, bacon edge up.
Gravy in a jug on the side, not poured over.
A spoon of cranberry sauce at the end of the platter.

why.0-0: A dry surface browns; a wet one steams. Leaving the netting on keeps the roast round so it cooks evenly.
why.0-3: The onion lifts the roast off the pan and flavours the drippings that become the gravy.
why.0-4: Broth in the pan stops the drippings from burning in a hot oven.
why.2-1: Cooking the flour in butter first takes away the raw taste and stops lumps.

funFact: Turkey breast is very lean, so it's done the moment it reaches 74°C. Every minute past that dries it out, which is why the thermometer matters more than the clock.

keeps.note: slice it and freeze with a little gravy so it stays moist

pairs: cheesy and rich beside lean turkey
